item.title: Network Automation Engineer
item.description:
🔌 QA Automation Engineer (Networking): Test the Switches That Power Data Centers

 

The challenge:

Every cloud service, every stream, every transaction travels through a data center network, and somewhere in that network, a switch has to forward the right packet to the right place, every single time.

 

Our client builds networking technology for data center infrastructure. Its software implements Layer 2 and Layer 3 switching and routing: VLANs, forwarding, tunneling, traffic controls, and more. Validation has to cover multiple software layers, physical and virtual devices, and successive generations of hardware.

 

And “can we configure the switch?” is only the beginning. You’ll need to prove that features behave correctly, that existing capabilities stay compatible, and that new functionality and performance targets are met. That takes engineers who understand how switches and routers work beneath the configuration layer, both to design effective tests and to find out why something failed.

 

Your role:

You’ll join a distributed Automation and QA team as an individual contributor, owning your work from the first feature discussion through planning, implementation, review, and long-term maintenance. item.title: QA Lead
item.description:
About the project:

A founder-led US healthtech startup — run by clinicians — is building an AI-powered mobile app for caregivers of children with complex medical needs. The app combines structured health tracking, EHR integration via SMART on FHIR, and an LLM-based assistant that remembers a child’s full history. It handles sensitive health data across multiple caregivers and profiles, with a layered permissions model. Public launch is planned for late November, and the quality and release process needs to be production-ready before that happens.

 

A new team member will be in charge of:

  • Own the end-to-end QA process — define the release baseline, give go/no-go decisions, and keep a short release record with residual risk documented each cycle.
  • Rebuild and tier the regression suite: remove duplicates, maintain one authoritative test repository, and trace requirements to tests and defects for high-risk areas like permissions, health data, and integrations.
  • Own AI feature testing — build and maintain eval datasets, check hallucination, exact-number recall, correct profile attribution, and context isolation between caregivers; define regression triggers for prompt, model, and config changes.
  • Drive mobile and web test automation — own the Maestro baseline for Flutter iOS/Android, maintain pipeline execution and reliability metrics, and extend web automation where it delivers real value.
